key_insight: Lower-star persistent homology on tennis competitive networks captures meaningful match structure and improves prediction beyond rankings alone.
engineering_relevance: The paper shows that topological and graph-derived features can be integrated into a practical predictive pipeline for sports analytics when traditional signals are incomplete or unavailable.
method: Build player competition networks and apply lower-star filtration to extract persistent homology summaries (VAB, HNAV, HWNAV, OW-HNPV).
Use Modified Band Depth plus optimized graph approximations to scale feature extraction to ~66k ATP matches.
Train Random Forest and compare against a modified Katz similarity model with temporal edge weighting.
evidence_signal: On ATP singles matches from 2000-2025, the combined model reached 66.2% accuracy (AUC 0.719), while topology-only still achieved 63.56% accuracy.
watch_item: Performance depends on careful network construction and approximation choices, so edge-weighting, filtration design, and temporal leakage must be validated to avoid overstating generalization.
paper_title: Topological Data Analysis and Graph-Theoretic Approaches for Tennis Match Prediction
